domestic.debt_note: 6M T-bill cutoff (2026-07-23 auction) sits at 11.79%, above the 11.5% policy rate for the first time this cycle, raising Rs768.4bn (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017647/govt-raises-rs768bn-via-treasury-bills-auction) -- market pricing hold-or-hike risk into the 2026-07-27 MPC. 10Y PIB unchanged at 11.69% (2026-07-02 auction, no fresher PIB auction found this run) (https://mettisglobal.news/SBP-raises-Rs615bn-in-Fixed-Rate-PIB-Auction-61543). Separately, S&P Global upgraded Pakistan's long-term sovereign credit rating to 'B' from 'B-' on 2026-07-22 (stable outlook, highest since 2019), citing fiscal consolidation and rebuilt external buffers under the IMF programme -- a genuine structural positive that has NOT offset the acute oil/conflict shock hitting the tape this week (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017530).
domestic.remittances: June 2026 monthly remittances fell 18.3% MoM to $3.5bn (from May's record $4.25bn), though still +2% YoY vs June 2025's $3.406bn; FY26 full year closed at a record $41.6bn (+8.6% YoY) (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2617441/remittances-hit-415b-without-structured-support, https://www.brecorder.com/news/amp/40429234).
domestic.current_account: June 2026 swung to a $649mn monthly deficit (from May's $500mn surplus) on higher imports and the MoM drop in remittances, closing FY26 at a marginal full-year $139mn deficit (vs FY25's $1.84bn surplus) despite record remittances -- SBP notes this remained within its projected 0-1% of GDP range (https://mmnews.tv/pakistan-posts-649-million-current-account-deficit-in-june-2026/, https://dailytimes.com.pk/1524687/pakistan-posts-139m-current-account-deficit-despite-record-remittances-in-fy26/).

global_read: global.json (11:22) shows the oil/conflict shock still running hot: Brent $99.93 (-0.75% 1d but +35.52% 1mo -- consolidating just under the $100 handle it cleared this week), VIX 18.7 (+12.38% 1d), S&P -1.21%, Dow -0.97%. PKR 277.92 and DXY 101.44 are comparatively steady, but a near-$100 Brent tape into a current account that just swung to a $649mn monthly deficit (June) is a genuine imported-inflation and reserves risk landing four days before the 2026-07-27 MPC. Global risk appetite remains risk-off in sympathy with the Houthi Red Sea tanker attacks and US-Iran escalation the desk's geo-risk and macro lenses have been tracking all week.
drivers: KSE-100 closed lower for a third straight session on 2026-07-23, shedding 2,690.48 points (-1.54%) to settle at 171,739.45 -- selling was broad-based across banks, fertilizer, E&P, OMCs, power and refineries, driven by the Houthi Red Sea tanker-attack escalation and renewed US-Iran tension (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619926/psx-ends-lower-for-third-straight-session, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40431400/volatility-at-bourse-kse-100-down-1300-points)

Brent crude is trading near/above the $100 handle after Houthi militants attacked tankers in the Red Sea (claiming a blockade-enforcement operation against Saudi ports) and President Trump threatened to extend US strikes on Iran -- a fresh escalation front layered on top of the existing Strait-of-Hormuz risk (https://www.businesstoday.in/world/story/brent-hits-100-as-tanker-attacks-hormuz-risks-put-crude-traders-on-edge-amid-us-iran-tensions-544913-2026-07-23, https://oilprice.com/Energy/Oil-Prices/Oil-Prices-Climb-Toward-100-as-Red-Sea-Risks-Rise.html)

S&P Global upgraded Pakistan's long-term sovereign credit rating to 'B' from 'B-' on 2026-07-22 (stable outlook, T&C rating also to 'B'), the highest level in nearly nine years, citing IMF-programme reform progress, fiscal consolidation (FY27 deficit projected ~4% of GDP, down from ~8% in crisis years) and rebuilt external buffers (reserves incl. gold cited at $25.3bn end-June, vs $6.7bn Dec-2022) -- a carried-forward structural positive that domestic conditions are improving even as the external oil/conflict shock dominates this week's tape (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017530, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619639/sp-upgrades-pakistans-credit-rating-to-b-from-b-highest-in-eight-years)

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, 11:22) reads 69/100 'elevated' -- energy-shock and conflict/escalation sub-factors both still pinned at 100/100 stress; the radar's own read argues for smaller size, defensives, and patience on new longs even with the domestic rating upgrade in hand (state/georisk.json)

SBP's 2026-07-27 MPC (3 days out) is still expected to hold at 11.5% per a 97% Topline Securities analyst poll, re-verified this run -- rationale is heightened geopolitical uncertainty plus the oil-price rebound offsetting otherwise well-contained inflation (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/21/sbp-likely-to-keep-interest-rate-unchanged/, https://www.bolnews.com/business/sbp-expected-to-hold-interest-rate-steady-amid-geopolitical-uncertainty-poll-shows/)

6M T-bill cutoff rose to 11.79% at the 2026-07-23 auction -- above the 11.5% policy rate for the first time this cycle -- signalling the market is pricing hold-or-hike risk into the MPC amid the intensifying oil/conflict shock (https://www.dawn.com/news/2017647/govt-raises-rs768bn-via-treasury-bills-auction)

SBP-held FX reserves stood at $17.26bn as of 2026-07-17 (down from $18.47bn on 2026-07-03 after a $1.245bn debt-repayment drawdown mid-month); total liquid reserves (incl. commercial banks) were $22.67bn -- distinct from S&P's broader $25.3bn 'incl. gold' figure cited for end-June (https://www.thenews.pk/print/1424970-sbp-forex-reserves-rise-1-9bn-to-18-47bn-as-of-july-3, https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/09/sbp-reserves-roar-back-near-19-billion-after-huge-increase/amp/)

CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 (from 11.7% in May); the disinflation trend predates this oil episode -- the July print (due 2026-08-01) is the first to carry daily fuel-price pass-through from the current Brent/Red Sea shock, a live upside risk (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428129/june-cpi-inflation-up-111pc-yoy)

June 2026 current account swung to a $649mn monthly deficit (from May's $500mn surplus) as remittances fell 18.3% MoM to $3.5bn off May's record $4.25bn -- FY26 closed at a marginal $139mn full-year deficit despite record $41.6bn annual remittances (https://mmnews.tv/pakistan-posts-649-million-current-account-deficit-in-june-2026/)

IMF EFF/RSF 4th review still has no confirmed date; last completed review (3rd EFF/2nd RSF, 2026-05-08) disbursed a combined ~$1.3bn, with both sides targeting a strategic framework signing around the September 2026 UNGA sidelines -- unchanged and re-verified this run (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf)

Net regime read: the acute Houthi tanker-attack/US-Iran escalation is still the dominant force on the tape -- three straight KSE-100 losing sessions, Brent holding near $100, VIX +12% and georisk still 'elevated' at 69/100 -- and it outweighs the genuinely positive S&P sovereign upgrade and steady MPC-hold consensus. Domestic anchors (rating upgrade, contained CPI trend, hold expectation) argue against a deeper risk-off spiral but do not flip the call; T-bill yields above policy rate and a current account back in deficit reinforce caution into the 07-27 MPC. Regime held at risk-off

favored: banks (T-bill yields above the 11.5% policy rate into the 07-27 MPC, and the S&P sovereign upgrade is a direct credit-quality tailwind for bank balance sheets/funding costs)
E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI -- direct beneficiaries of Brent holding near $100)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta)
avoid: OMCs (current account back in monthly deficit, faster fuel-price pass-through compounds margin-timing/circular-debt risk on a sustained oil tape)
cement (energy-cost sensitive; input-cost pressure evident even before this fresh oil leg)
textiles/exporters (current account swung back to deficit in June; Red Sea/Bab-al-Mandab freight-route risk now directly live via the Houthi tanker attacks)
